setup.system: You are an assistant to a traffic engineer. Answer questions from the SUMO simulation of the Fowler Ave corridor by calling the tools yourself: the engineer cannot call them. Keep calling tools until you can answer. Do not guess numbers.

question: Is Fowler Ave westbound at 30th St spilling back during the PM peak hour?

function.name: list_intersections
function.description: List every signalized intersection in the network, named by its cross streets, with each approach's direction of travel (EB/WB/NB/SB), lanes at the stop line, speed limit in mph, and storage length in feet (stop line back to the previous signal or the network edge). Use these names in the other tools; you never need SUMO's internal ids. Reads the network file only; no simulation runs.

function.name: start_live
function.description: Start one live SUMO simulation of the Fowler Ave scenario that the other live tools then read and change. gui=True opens SUMO's graphical window (sumo-gui) so people can watch, for example in a TMC; gui=False runs headless, which is faster and is what you want for long or repeated runs (and the only choice on a computer without a screen, such as a server). The clock starts at 0 s; the first 900 s are warm-up and the analysis hour is 900-4500 s. Starting a new one closes any running simulation.

function.name: advance
function.description: Run the live simulation FORWARD by this many seconds (1-3600), relative to now; a change you made (a new signal timing) acts only while time passes. Returns the vehicle ledger for the interval: vehicles that entered and left, the change in vehicles in the network (always entered minus left), how many are waiting to enter at the network edge, and teleports. SUMO teleports a vehicle stuck for 300 s by moving it ahead: any teleport means the network jammed somewhere and travel times are no longer physical.

function.name: get_approach_state
function.description: Traffic on one approach to a signal, over the whole block (stop line back to the previous signal), as of the last simulation step. intersection: cross streets, e.g. "Fowler & McKinley"; approach: EB, WB, NB or SB (direction of travel). Returns: vehicles on the block; stopped vehicles (below 0.1 m/s); back of queue in feet and vehicles in it, where a vehicle is queued if slower than 5 km/h (3.1 mph) and within 10 m of the queue ahead in any lane (SUMO's lane-area detector rule); storage length, and a verdict: SPILLBACK when the queue fills over 85% of it, otherwise "No spillback", with the share either way; space-mean speed in mph, the average of the vehicles' speeds, or "no vehicles" when the block is empty (speed is undefined at zero density; SUMO's lane speed would report the speed limit); density in veh/mi/lane; and the through signal indication. A queue at a signal rises and falls every cycle: one reading is a snapshot, so read it at the end of red or several times. A reading outside the analysis hour (900-4500 s) carries a WARM-UP or AFTER-PEAK warning: it says nothing about the peak. Read-only.

function.name: stop_live
function.description: Close the live simulation, if one is running.
